diagnosis.reason:
SCOPE: Diagnosed and attempted repair of the vibration-powered monitoring node (main beam = 45 Hz background harvester; auxiliary beam + RC envelope = wake detector; MCU polls at 100 ms / comparator gate; 1.8 V brownout). Used all 3 observations up front and all 3 full evaluations; no fast/numeric evaluator is qualified, so I can no longer change the design. The design left in place is main 26 mm, aux 20 mm, C 80 µF, gate 2.0 V, threshold 0.55 V — still 0/4 delivered.

DIAGNOSIS (from the one full observation of the initial design):
1) Supply/power is the primary fault. Storage never exceeds 0.128 V (brownout 1.8 V); only 1.6e-6 J reaches the cap. Main-beam peak is 0.486 V, i.e. right at the ~0.5 V rectifier knee, so almost no charge passes. Total mechanical input (4.2e-5 J over 30 s) is ~200x below a resonant harvester, so the main 45 Hz harvester is far off-resonance — consistent with the stated unmeasured effective-length variation detuning it. 150 µF was also oversized (V ∝ 1/√C).
2) Trigger can’t cross on its own: aux/envelope reaches only 1.19 V while the gate’s floor is 2.0 V (init 2.9 V), so the comparator path can never fire; delivery therefore depends on the 100 ms MCU polling fallback, which itself only works once the node is powered.
3) Program is downstream: MCU never powered (MCU_input = 0, no stages executed).

WHAT I TRIED AND WHY IT FAILED: I lowered C to its 80 µF floor and gate to its 2.0 V floor (both strictly helpful), then swept the main beam: longer (34, 40 mm) and shorter (26 mm). All three still returned 0 delivered, so the realized main-beam resonance (sharply peaked, Q ~20–50) was never actually placed on the 45 Hz band within my attempts. I over-spent the three full evaluations on bracketing before locating the resonant length, and I had already consumed all observations, so I could not measure the resonant peak/main_peak to finish the compensation.

REMAINING UNCERTAINTY: the sign and magnitude of the effective-length offset (needed to set the nominal main length exactly onto realized 45 Hz), and whether the 2.0 V gate floor can even be crossed by the aux envelope (a lower gate is not allowed by the domain), i.e. whether wake must be achieved at all or the polling fallback suffices once powered. I did not reach full-service success.

DID NOT ACHIEVE FULL-SERVICE SUCCESS (0/4 delivered in every evaluated design). Root-cause diagnosis and what remains unresolved:

1) Binding failure is POWER, not the radio/program logic. Storage peaks at ~0.128 V versus the 1.8 V brownout; MCU_input energy = 0. Rectified-to-storage is only ~1.58 µJ against the ~130–243 µJ needed to charge 80–150 µF to 1.8 V (~100–150× short). Mechanical damping (~33 µJ) dwarfs the converted electrical energy (~1.6 µJ), the classic signature of a high-Q beam sitting far off resonance with any strong input — i.e., the unmeasured effective-length variation detuned a beam.

2) Trigger is a second, coupled blocker. The envelope peaks at 1.19 V but gate_V's domain floor is 2.0 V. If the gate is the wake comparator, no allowed gate setting can ever be reached (envelope can't hit 2.0 V as-is), so the envelope would have to be lifted above 2.0 V by tuning the aux beam onto the 210 Hz target. If instead threshold_V=0.55 is the comparator (envelope ≫ 0.55), wake is fine and power is the sole blocker. This ambiguity in which variable gates the wake could not be resolved without another observation.

3) Interventions tried (all returned 0/0/0 delivered/false/brownout): main 24 mm; main 36 mm; aux 16 mm — each with C=80 µF, gate=2.0 V, threshold=0.55 V. None reached resonance, so neither the varied-beam identity (main vs aux) nor the offset direction/magnitude was pinned down.

Remaining uncertainty / needed next step: the realized natural frequency of the varied beam is unknown. I ran out of the observation budget (intended for exactly this: a length sweep reading main_peak/aux_peak/envelope) on the initial three channel reads, and exhausted the 3 full evaluations before bracketing the resonance. To finish reliably one must: sweep the suspect beam length while observing power (find where mechanical/electrical output jumps), then set the power beam to realize ~45 Hz (sustained 0.15 g background → hundreds of µJ over 30 s) and set the aux beam to realize 210 Hz with envelope > 2.0 V, keep C at the 80 µF floor for fast threshold climb, pin gate at 2.0 V, and choose threshold_V so 210 Hz wakes/delivers while the spectral confirm rejects the 250 Hz/0.8 g nuisance (avoiding false reports). Without that frequency information, further blind length guesses are unlikely to hit the narrow resonance band. Note: the currently committed design (main 30 / aux 16 / C 80 / gate 2.0 / threshold 0.55) is a failing state, not a solution.

SCOPE: Axis-2 monitoring node, 4-event service. Result: NOT achieved — final executed design delivered 0/4 with 0 false reports.

DIAGNOSIS (from the three measurements on the initial design):
- Power/supply is healthy: storage reached max 3.30 V, cold-charge ready ~7.1 s, brownouts 0, main-beam peak 4.25 V. Main beam + rectifier are not the fault.
- The failure is the trigger front-end. Auxiliary peak voltage was only 0.160 V, the RC envelope stayed 0.00 V, and the MCU had 0 wakeups (program stage counters all 0). So no event is ever sensed or gated — consistent with terminal "delivery alone does not identify cause": here the cause is upstream of the MCU.
- Root cause: the auxiliary beam is mechanically off the 210 Hz target resonance (the unmeasured effective-length variation), so its PZT output never exceeds the rectifier/envelope diode drop and the comparator never fires. Low gate/threshold can't help because the envelope itself is zero.

INTERVENTIONS TRIED (all full fidelity, delivered 0/4 each): aux_length = 24, 15, 16.5 mm with gate 2.0–2.9 V and thresholds 0.2–0.45 V. No length in 15–24 mm produced any envelope even at a 0.2 V threshold, which rules out that range and, since 24 mm (longest → lowest resonance) also failed, indicates the realized resonance is at a SHORTER length than 15 mm (most likely ~12–14 mm).

REMAINING UNCERTAINTY: The exact compensating aux length was not confirmed because the 3 full-evaluation budget was spent before testing the short-length region, and the correct amplitude-splitting gate/threshold values remain unmeasured. I therefore cannot certify a fully passing configuration; the current design (aux 16.5 mm) still yields 0/4. Recommended next step (if budget existed): set aux_length ≈ 12–14 mm and re-tune threshold to sit between the on-resonance 210 Hz target response and the off-resonance 250 Hz nuisance response.

SCOPE & OUTCOME: Task not fully satisfied — 0/4 delivered remained through every executed configuration (full-eval budget exhausted: aux length 13.5, 14.0, 16.0 mm trials, plus gate/threshold lowering). No false reports, no brownouts in any run.

ROOT CAUSE (well supported): Power is healthy (storage ~3.30 V sustained, cold-charge 7.1 s, main beam 4.25 V) — only the TRIGGER FRONT-END fails. Measured aux_peak = 0.16 V, envelope_peak = 0.0 V (exact zero → the RC-envelope branch never charges above the rectifier drop / is inactive), wakeups = 0, so the MCU never wakes/samples/TXs → 0 deliveries.

COMPETING HYPOTHESES (explicitly kept):
1) Mechanical mistuning: aux resonance off 210 Hz. I tested shorter lengths (13.5/14/16 mm). All 0 delivered. Soft EI / composite-stiffness estimate puts nominal 18 mm ≈185–205 Hz, and the stated unmeasured effective-length variation could offset ±~2 mm (resonance ~175 or ~262 Hz) — BOTH fit the 0.16 V reading, so the SIGN of the length offset remains unresolved; my shorter trials did not hit it, leaving "~16 mm (nominal low-E case or +offset)" vs "~20 mm (realized-shorter case)" as the two live length branches.
2) Circuit/threshold (now the LEADING untested lead): because envelope is flat 0 while aux = 0.16 V, the comparator very likely gates on the RAW aux peak, and threshold_V=0.55 sat ABOVE the available 0.16 V signal — the knob floor (0.15 V) lies just below that 0.16 V peak, strongly suggesting the intended trip point. Setting threshold_V=0.15 with gate_V≈2.0 is the highest-probability repair and was NOT testable within budget.

RECOMMENDED NEXT INTERVENTION (bounded, unverified): restore aux to nominal 18 mm, set threshold_V=0.15 (below the measured 0.16 V peak), gate_V=2.0, keep C=150 µF; rely on the digital 128-pt/2048 Hz spectral CONFIRM to reject the 250 Hz/0.8 g nuisance (its larger amplitude will over-wake the analog stage, but CONFIRM should block false TX). If that does not trip, then the aux is genuinely mistuned and a length sweep is required.

REMAINING UNCERTAINTY: (a) sign/magnitude of the unmeasured aux effective-length offset (resonance ~175 vs ~262 Hz), unresolved by the 0.16 V magnitude alone; (b) whether the comparator reads the raw aux peak (favoring threshold reduction) or a rectified/other node; (c) whether, once tripping works, 150 µF storage sustains 4 full wake/sample/confirm/TX cycles without brownout (brownouts were 0 so far, but no TX-load has been exercised). Numerical uncertainty in resonance is large (±20%) due to effective PZT stiffness and clamping.

Diagnosis: the initial node is essentially tuned near the 210 Hz fault, so the 2 g fault creates the excessive stress/travel; the first candidate over-detuned to ~369 Hz and lost charging. The later 5 g/1.06h test confirmed stress/travel still fail because it remained near the 210 Hz resonance. My intended final redesign is: A=true, mass_g=4.45, h=1.10, C_uF=100, gate_V=2.5, discharge_Mohm=20, wake_V=0.45, input_series_kohm=0.5, poll_ms=100. This should move the main resonance to ~248 Hz (lower target response and stress while retaining 45 Hz background charging) and use the auxiliary front end plus a lower comparator threshold for target wakeup. Remaining uncertainty: no full-evaluation budget remained to verify this final candidate, so full-service success was not demonstrated; the last measured design still fails stress/travel.

SCOPE / OUTCOME: I did not achieve a validated full-service pass. All three full evaluations (plus the initial full-transient baseline) failed delivery, and the full-design budget is now exhausted (0 full designs remaining; fast evaluation is not available), so I cannot re-test. The node design currently on record is the last attempted one (mass 5.0 g, h 0.95), which is NOT recommended because it never reaches gate voltage.

DIAGNOSIS (fairly firm):
- The failures are spectral, not energy/trigger-count. The baseline has no brownouts (min active storage 2.31 V), yet all 3 wakeups sampled and were REJECTed with 0 CONFIRM and both faults (8.0 s, 10.0 s) missed.
- I tested the "energy/re-arm/peek" hypothesis (default mechanics, discharge 1 MΩ, wake 0.5 V, peek on): wakeups jumped 3→34 and cold-charge improved to 5.86 s, but still 0 confirmed and both faults missed. So waking/sampling more does not help — the 128-point/2048 Hz (16 Hz bins) classifier simply does not see the 210 Hz/0.5 g fault dominate over the continuous 250 Hz/0.8 g nuisance.
- The decisive structural finding: the harvester is sharply resonant with its default drive. Both down-shifts of resonance collapsed harvested power and never charged: (h=0.9, mass 5.0) → final 0.51 V; (mass 5.0, h=0.95) → final 0.99 V, wakeups 0. So the allowed mass/h ranges cannot move resonance into 195–225 Hz while keeping the charger alive. This is the core tension: to make 210 Hz beat 250 Hz in the sampled spectrum the harvester must be resonant near 210, but the energy source is tied to the default resonance, so retuning starves the node.

BEST-SUPPORTED REPAIR (recommended, NOT validated — revert the current mass 5.0/h 0.95 setting):
- Keep mechanics at the power-optimal default: mass_g 4.65, h 1.0 (only configuration that reliably charges; stress/travel have large headroom).
- Keep C 150 µF, gate 2.9 V (no-brownout proven).
- Enable the intended software precheck: peek_ms ≈ 2–3 ms, peek_threshold_g ≈ 0.25 (skips the lossy cold-start/background acquisition that competes with the first fault for charge).
- Moderate envelope discharge (≈ 8–15 MΩ) to re-arm between the 2 s-spaced events without comparator chatter/flooding (discharge 1 MΩ caused 34-wake nuisance flooding; 20 MΩ may not re-arm).
- Lower trigger (wake_V ≈ 0.4) and faster poll (≈ 40 ms) so the 0.15 s, 0.5 g fault is captured inside the 0.25 s deadline; low bridge series (≈ 1 kΩ) for charging.

REMAINING UNCERTAINTY: (1) Whether the unchanged classifier can ever confirm a 0.5 g/210 Hz fault given the 0.8 g/250 Hz nuisance and the harvester's resonance constraint — this may require accepting a resonance compromise I could not find within the mass/h limits. (2) Whether the fault falls inside the 62.5 ms acquisition window given wake/boot latency (lower wake_V to trigger near fault onset is the main untested lever). (3) My resonance/charging inference comes from only two detuning data points with an unknown damping model; a proper frequency-response probe (numeric sweep of mass/h vs harvested power and CONFIRM rate) is the needed next step before committing parameters.

SCOPE: Self-powered vibration node must deliver 2 in-band (195–225 Hz) target events (faults at t=8.0 s and t=10.0 s, 0.5 g, deadline 0.25 s) with a small initial energy buffer, while rejecting 45 Hz background / 250 Hz nuisance, avoiding brownout (1.8 V), stress ≤40 MPa, travel ≤1.5 mm. Budget: 3 full evaluations used (fast evaluator unavailable), so the corrected design below could not be validated.

DIAGNOSIS (from measurements):
1. Baseline failure = energy, not signal. Every wake did WAKE→SAMPLE→BROWNOUT (8/8), never CONFIRM/TX. Confirmed by program/trigger/power observations.
2. Harvest power is ~100 µW and is harvester-limited, essentially independent of the diode-bridge series resistance (86 µW at 5 kΩ → 100 µW at 0.5 kΩ). So series R only gives a small gain.
3. Sample+classify cycle costs ~290 µJ (measured: 200 µF dropped 2.90→2.35 V). With a 2 s re-arm gap the harvester returns ~200 µJ, so storage must absorb the deficit — the buffer must be sized accordingly, not tiny.
4. The default geometry is ALREADY the 45 Hz harvest resonance (peak harvest). Proof: h=0.9/m=5.0 crashed power (V_oc≈0.43 V, tip 0.107 mm), and h=1.02 dropped open-circuit voltage to ≈2.81 V — below the 2.9 V gate, so the node never armed (0 wakeups). ⇒ do NOT change mass/h; any detune lowers power/V_oc.
5. Because V_oc is only a little above 2.9 V, gate_V must stay ≤~2.9 V and C must be scaled so arm_time = 0.5·C·gate²/P < 8 s with margin. The 200 µF run armed at 8.408 s (too late → missed fault 1, but delivered fault 2 cleanly, proving the rest works once armed). There is no forced "boot sample"; a sample only follows a comparator trigger.

RECOMMENDED PASSING DESIGN (derived, not run due to budget): A=false; mass_g=4.65; h=1.0; C_uF≈165; gate_V=2.9; input_series_kohm=0.5; wake_V=0.55; discharge_Mohm=20; poll_ms=100. Predicted: arms ~6.9 s (<8 s); fault1 triggers at 8.0 s and is confirmed/TX within ~0.15 s; 2 s re-arm refills and fault2 triggers at 10.0 s; minimum active storage ~1.9 V (>1.8 V, no brownout); stress ~15.5 MPa; tip ~0.4 mm; classifier rejects 45/250 Hz (no false reports).

REMAINING UNCERTAINTY: (a) exact V_oc margin above gate at default geometry — if V_oc is closer to 2.9 V, arm time lengthens and C should be trimmed to ~150 µF; (b) whether any stray 250 Hz nuisance in the short arm→8 s window fires a wasted ~290 µJ sample (would need slightly larger C or a lower wake_V); (c) enabling the auxiliary front end (A=true) could cut per-event energy and add margin but its trigger threshold/rearm behavior is unverified here.

Scope: P2_unit_u four-event receiver. Diagnosis: the dominant failure is the main power beam, not the aux trigger front end. Initial power data and the 250 Hz peak-tip/stress are consistent with a much shorter realized effective main length, moving its resonance far above the 45 Hz background; the 150 uF storage and 2.9 V gate also prevent boot. Best bounded repair (not full-transient verified because the third full-design budget was exhausted): main_length_mm=42.0 (upper bound, nearest attainable restoration of the 45 Hz power resonance), aux_length_mm=18.0 (aux remains at its 210 Hz nominal), C_uF=80.0, gate_V=2.0, threshold_V=0.4. Remaining uncertainty: the exact effective-length offset is approximately -12 to -14 mm; 42 mm is the closest legal main setting, so residual detuning may remain. The last executed design was main_length_mm=27.0, which failed; it should not be used.

SCOPE / DIAGNOSIS
- Power side is healthy: storage charges to ~3.30 V (main peak 4.25 V, cold-ready 7 s, ~0.0036 J into storage), zero brownouts. This is NOT a power problem.
- The failure is entirely in the TRIGGER front-end. Measured trigger internals on the initial design: aux_peak = 0.16 V, envelope_peak = 0.0 V, wakeups = 0. The program stage counters are all zero (WAKE/SAMPLE/CONFIRM/TX = 0), i.e. the MCU never samples because the comparator never fires. Root cause: the auxiliary beam's voltage (0.16 V) is below the diode-rectifier turn-on, so the RC envelope stays at 0 and never crosses the 0.55 V comparator threshold — hence 0/4 delivered with 0 false reports.

WHAT WAS TRIED (all full transient, all delivered 0, false 0, brownout 0)
1) aux_length 24 mm (max) — no delivery.
2) aux_length 24 mm + threshold 0.15 V (floor) + gate 2.0 V — still no delivery; even the minimum comparator threshold is not reached, so the rectified envelope stays essentially 0 at 24 mm. This rules out the "just lower the threshold / lengthen for more deflection" hypothesis: under a quasi-static (stiff) beam model the lengthening only raises aux to ~0.4 V, still below rectifier turn-on.
3) aux_length 20 mm + threshold 0.2 V + gate 2.0 V — no delivery.

STRONGEST REMAINING HYPOTHESIS / REPAIR PATH
The aux beam is detuned by the "unmeasured effective-length variation," so it is not delivering a resonant (multi-volt) burst that can rectify into the envelope. The real fix is to retune the aux nominal length so the realized aux beam resonates at the 210 Hz target (giving a large, and frequency-selective, signal that also rejects the 250 Hz nuisance), combined with threshold near the 0.15 V floor and gate ~2.0 V for sag margin. I only sampled lengths ≥18 mm (18/20/24 all fail); the compensating length most likely lies on the shorter side (~11–16 mm) that I never got to test.

REMAINING UNCERTAINTY
Full-evaluation budget (3) is exhausted and fast/observation budgets are unavailable, so I could not pinpoint the resonant aux length or confirm a delivering configuration. Delivery was NOT achieved within budget; the confirmed-failing last design is aux_length 20 mm / threshold 0.2 V / gate 2.0 V. Recommended next action: sweep aux_length over the shorter half of [11,24] mm (with threshold ≈0.15 V, gate ≈2.0 V, C≈150 µF) using the trigger observation (aux_peak / envelope_peak / wakeups) to locate the resonance, then lock that length in.
